trickyParts: A reopen cannot be told from another status move by status alone, so issue events now name closed_at in changed on a close or reopen; the client refreshes the whole Inbox and the project badges only then.

thread_logins on a status move names only logins with a Replies row on the issue's open asks (what myRepliesUnread can move), read through asks_open and user_threads_thread, so no scan of user_threads.

The scheduler counts a refresh as paid by any fetch that starts after it was asked for; a first-loading query's predicate runs on the landed body; nothing is ever cancelled (DispatchQueryClient covers mutation invalidations too).
The budget test's barrier renames the open issue until its detail is read again and the header shows the new title, so it works at both commits and under INFRA-258's transport.
A `when` test decided while any fetch is out waits for the landed response; a refetch that fails is judged on the data it leaves on screen, so a refresh is never dropped for good.

A query left while it owes a refresh is marked stale again after the in-flight fetch settles, since that fetch cleared the stale flag; the summary reads are staleTime Infinity, so without this they stayed wrong until the next event.

#2210's block links read the block's graph read (blockQuery) and the issue summary for a pinned spec block's path; references_changed names cited blocks only when some source cites them, so a large spec rewrite does not hit the cap of 20.

The contracts zod schemas list the new fields, so agents' parsed issue, message and ask notifications carry changed, ancestors and thread_logins (comment payloads already passed them through).
